//: Keyboard-mode shortcuts. How the mode is entered is controlled by
"trigger" (also switchable in Theme settings):
"auto" — on whenever nothing is focused for typing (default; today's behavior)
"esc"  — only Escape enters the mode; blur does not
null   — keyboard mode disabled
Inside the mode the keys work on their own, with no modifier. Edit this
file and reload the tab to change them — it is read once at startup
(Theme settings writes "trigger" live without a reload).
This file holds OVERRIDES only for key bindings, and ships with an empty
bindings object: the shipped keymap lives in SLICC itself, so whatever
you do not mention here follows it, including any keys a later version
adds. Press ? in keyboard mode to see what is bound.
Each entry is "key": "command". A key is a single character ("x") or a named
key ("Enter", "Tab", "Backspace", "Delete", "Home", "End", "ArrowLeft",
"ArrowRight", "ArrowUp", "ArrowDown"). Several keys may share one command.
A command with no key left is simply unreachable from the keyboard.
To REMOVE a binding, set it to null. Deleting a line does NOT remove the key —
it restores whatever SLICC ships for it.
Commands: composer, nextAgent, prevAgent, newConversation,
newConversationErase, newCone, dropCone, sessions, stop, approvals, attach,
copyReply, copyChat, voice, nextItem, prevItem, leftRail, rightRail, files,
tabs, peek, terminal, memory, monitor, sprinkles, zoom, model, cycleModel,
cycleThinking, accounts, help.
Some commands own a list, and the keys pressed straight after them address
THAT list instead of the tab strip: files, memory, sessions and sprinkles.
A digit picks from it (f 3 is the third file, r 9 the oldest archived chat —
9 is always the last one, exactly as it is for agents), and nextItem /
prevItem page through it, looping. With no list open they are next/previous
message in the transcript instead. The list stays addressable for as long as
its keys are still showing on the pill above the composer.
Esc and the digits 1-9 are reserved: Esc is the mode itself, and the digits
address the tab strip by position (9 is always the last agent).
Example — the SLICC 6.110 keyboard, if you had it in your fingers. Note
that v1 spent "e" on the terminal, where the shipped map now has
sprinkles, and "t" on the browser rather than the terminal:
"bindings": {
"d": "nextAgent", "c": "composer", "n": "newConversation",
"b": "leftRail", "x": "rightRail", "f": "files", "t": "tabs",
"e": "terminal", "m": "memory", "s": "sprinkles",
"l": "model", "a": "accounts", "h": "help", "/": "help"
This file is yours — SLICC only writes it when it is missing, or when Theme
settings updates "trigger".
